failures.title: Mercedes M274 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Wear (Early Models)
items.whatHappens: Early production M274 engines (roughly 2012-2015) inherited a timing chain tensioner vulnerability from the outgoing M271 family. The tensioner can fail to maintain adequate hydraulic pressure, leading to chain stretch, a distinct metallic rattle on cold starts, and camshaft correlation fault codes. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth, causing catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, a full timing chain kit and updated tensioner replacement is viable. However, if the chain has already jumped and caused internal damage, a full Mercedes M274 engine replacement is the only reliable solution.

items.title: PCV Valve Diaphragm Failure and Oil Consumption
items.whatHappens: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve diaphragm can rupture over time, leading to a distinct whining noise from the valve cover, increased oil consumption, and a rough idle. In severe cases, the ruptured diaphragm draws excess oil vapour into the intake tract, fouling the intercooler, throttle body, and intake valves.
items.repairVsReplace: The PCV valve is integrated into the valve cover on the M274, meaning the entire valve cover must be replaced rather than just the diaphragm. This is a relatively straightforward repair and does not typically require engine replacement unless severe oil starvation has caused bottom-end bearing damage.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes M274
variants.intro: The M274 engine code (including sub-codes M274.920 and M274.921) is stamped directly onto a machined pad on the engine block, typically located near the oil filter housing or the bell housing. It is also clearly listed on your vehicle's V5C registration document under "Engine Number" and can be decoded from the full VIN. The M274.920 typically denotes the 184hp tune (C200/E200/GLC200), while the M274.921 denotes the higher-output 211hp/245hp tune (C250/E250/GLC300). Common Confusion Warning: Owners frequently confuse the longitudinal M274 with several other Mercedes 2.0L and 1.8L engines: - M270: The M270 is the transverse-mounted version of this engine, fitted to front-wheel-drive compact models (A-Class, B-Class, CLA, GLA). Fitting an M270 into a longitudinal W205 or W213 will result in severe mounting, exhaust, and wiring incompatibilities. - M264: The M264 is the direct successor in the W205 facelift and W213, featuring a 48V mild-hybrid system (ISG) and different engine mount points. While both are 2.0L longitudinal turbos, they are not direct swap replacements without extensive ECU and wiring modifications. - M271: The older 1.8L turbo/supercharged engine. While it shares some architectural DNA, the M271 has different displacement, mounting, and engine management systems.

relatives.description: / - The 1.8L turbocharged predecessor it replaced, which featured older port-injection or early direct-injection setups and suffered from different timing chain tensioner vulnerabilities.

- The direct 2.0L longitudinal successor introduced from 2017, which added a 48V mild-hybrid system (ISG) and revised engine mounts, making it physically incompatible as a direct swap despite the shared displacement.

- The transverse-mounted variant of this engine family, fitted to front-wheel-drive compact models like the A-Class and B-Class; owners of FWD platforms should check this page instead, as the M270 is not a direct physical swap.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement Mercedes M274 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Mercedes M274 is only advisable for lower-mileage host vehicles and *only* if accompanied by documented, stamped service history proving the timing chain and tensioner have been replaced with updated components. Without this history, the risk of inheriting the same catastrophic stretch issues on early models is unacceptably high.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the most recommended route for the M274. A proper reconditioned unit will include a brand-new timing chain kit, an updated tensioner, and a new valve cover with a fresh PCV diaphragm, directly addressing the engine's known weak points out of the box.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if your original M274 suffered a jumped timing chain that damaged the cylinder head, valves, or pistons, or if severe PCV failure caused oil starvation to the crankshaft bearings. A specialist rebuild will machine the block, fit updated timing components, and ensure all oil galleries are clear.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing a replacement is only half the job. Our network provides full supply and fit services, ensuring the engine is installed by Mercedes-specialist technicians with a nationwide warranty backing both the labour and the unit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: For core hosts like the W205 C-Class and X253 GLC, current UK market values typically sit between £8,000 and £25,000 . With a reconditioned M274 replacement costing from £3,800 (plus fitting), the repair cost generally represents 20-40% of the vehicle's value, making replacement financially viable. However, for early W204 C250 hosts valued under £5,000, we strongly advise evaluating the car's scrap or part-exchange value before committing to a full engine replacement.

items.question: What is the most common failure with the Mercedes M274 engine?
items.answer: The most documented failure pattern for the M274 is timing chain stretch and tensioner wear on early production models (2012-2015), typically occurring between 50,000 and 90,000 miles. → Get quotes for a rebuilt M274 with the timing chain and PCV failures already addressed.
